title: Participate in agri/ecotourism practices at both micro and meso levels to tourists

lessons.title: What agri-tourism and ecotourism are
lessons.html:
Tourism on the farm

Agri-tourism means bringing visitors to a working farm to experience farming. Examples are farm stays, fruit picking days, wine and cheese tastings, farm markets, tractor rides, school visits to see dairy cows milked, and festivals at harvest time.

Ecotourism means responsible travel to natural areas that protects the environment and benefits local people. Examples are guided walks in the veld, bird watching at a farm dam, game viewing on a farm with wildlife, hiking trails and mountain biking routes.

Why farms offer tourism

  • Extra income when farm income is low or uncertain, for example in drought years.
  • Jobs for local people as guides, cooks, cleaners, drivers and craft sellers.
  • Direct sales of farm products such as jam, honey, meat, fruit and vegetables.
  • Teaching visitors where food comes from and why conservation matters.
  • Support for the local economy: shops, transport and crafters.

Micro and meso levels

LevelMeaningExample
MicroOne farm or a small business serving touristsA family farm offering a farm-stay cottage and a strawberry picking morning
MesoSeveral farms, businesses and the community working together in a districtA farm route linking farm stalls, a dairy, a craft centre and B&Bs, with a shared map and marketing

Your role

As a farm worker you may help as a guide, help at the farm stall, prepare products, keep facilities clean or look after visitors' safety. You are the face of the farm. Visitors remember a friendly greeting, clear explanations and a clean, safe place.

lessons.title: Hosting tourists well and safely
lessons.html:
Good service to tourists

  • Greet visitors warmly and introduce yourself.
  • Speak clearly and simply. Many tourists know nothing about farming. Explain what you do and why.
  • Be patient with questions. If you do not know the answer, say so and find someone who does.
  • Respect visitors from all cultures and countries.
  • Be on time for tours and activities.
  • Wear clean clothes or the farm uniform and keep your name tag on.

Telling the farm's story

Tourists enjoy stories. Prepare a few simple points about the farm: its history, what is grown or farmed, how the seasons affect the work, interesting animals or plants, and how the farm looks after the veld and water. Local knowledge, such as the names of plants in your home language and their traditional uses, makes a tour special.

Keeping visitors safe

  • Give a short safety talk before an activity: stay with the group, keep children close, do not touch machinery or chemicals.
  • Keep visitors away from working tractors, bulls, dip tanks, chemical stores and deep dams.
  • Wash-hand stations should be used after touching animals, to reduce the risk of diseases passing from animals to people.
  • Know where the first aid box is and who is trained in first aid.
  • Know the emergency numbers and the farm's address for ambulances.
  • Watch for heat, sunburn, snakes and bees on walks.

Protecting the farm and nature

  • Keep visitors on paths and out of planted lands and closed camps.
  • Close gates behind the group.
  • Do not let visitors feed or chase animals.
  • Ask visitors not to pick wild flowers or remove plants.
  • Provide bins and collect litter.
  • Follow biosecurity rules, for example foot baths at pig or poultry units.

Key points

  • Agri-tourism shows visitors farming; ecotourism shows nature responsibly.
  • Micro level is one farm; meso level is farms and community working together.
  • Greet, explain simply and tell the farm's story.
  • Keep visitors away from machinery, chemicals, dangerous animals and deep water.
  • Close gates, keep to paths and follow biosecurity rules.

quiz.question: Which is an example of agri-tourism?

options.text: A strawberry picking day on a working farm
A visit to a car factory

quiz.question: What does tourism at the meso level mean?

options.text: One family farm offering a cottage
Several farms, businesses and the community working together in a district

quiz.question: A visitor asks a question you cannot answer. What should you do?

options.text: Tell them it is a silly question
Say you do not know and find someone who does

quiz.question: Why should visitors wash their hands after touching farm animals?

options.text: To reduce the risk of diseases passing from animals to people
Because the farm charges for water
To remove the smell from cameras

quiz.question: What should you do with gates when leading a group through camps?

options.text: Leave them open for the next group
